paths.description: Public entry URL in its current out-of-hours state; represents the only same-host page/template discoverable because all paths return this notice. Audited desktop, narrow mobile, dark, increased-contrast, reduced-motion, no-JS, performance, network, security, accessibility, and memory conditions. Authenticated/in-hours betting and external linked JRA services were not covered because they were not exposed by this host/state.

findings.summary: The service notice ignores the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is pixel-for-pixel equivalent in palette to the light capture; the body remains white and the notice panel remains light peach.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide dark surface, text, link, border, and alert colors through prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Important red status and recovery text fails WCAG AA contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse/axe reports both red #ff0000 spans on white at 3.99:1, below the required 4.5:1 for 16px normal text.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a darker alert red with at least 4.5:1 contrast on white and verify under increased-contrast/forced-colors conditions.

findings.summary: The page has no mobile viewport and is rendered as a 980px desktop canvas scaled down to 360px.
findings.evidence: At a 360x800 device viewport, layout reports clientWidth 980 and visual scale 0.367 because no viewport meta exists; the screenshot shows tiny text and controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Add width=device-width, initial-scale=1 and use fluid layout/type so content reflows at narrow widths without browser-wide downscaling.

findings.summary: A tiny static notice is delayed by document latency and uncached assets.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse records LCP 2.6s and a 740ms root response; HAR records the document at 2297ms and all three images missing cache headers despite only 15KB total transfer.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce origin response time, compress the HTML, and give versioned static images long-lived immutable caching while preserving no-store only where transaction state requires it.

findings.summary: The document has no main landmark.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe finds no header/nav/main/aside/footer landmarks, and Lighthouse reports landmark-one-main failure on the html element.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap the central notice in <main> and use semantic header/footer elements without disrupting the existing heading.

findings.summary: The response omits an HTML doctype and renders in quirks mode.
findings.evidence: The active DOM reports doctype null and compatMode BackCompat; Lighthouse’s doctype audit fails.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a valid <!doctype html>, modern UTF-8 charset metadata near the start of head, and standards-mode markup.

findings.summary: Every tested utility and nonexistent path returns the out-of-service HTML with HTTP 200.
findings.evidence: Direct HTTP probes show /robots.txt, /sitemap.xml, /manifest.webmanifest, and /nonexistent-audit-probe all return 200 text/html with the same notice; Lighthouse also reports bfcache disabled by no-store.
findings.suggestedFix: Return accurate 404/5xx status codes and content types for unavailable resources, provide a real error page, and scope no-store to genuinely sensitive responses.

findings.summary: The page has no meta description.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe reports description null and Lighthouse’s meta-description audit fails, although the title is present.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a concise Japanese meta description that explains this is the JRA internet voting status/entry page.

findings.summary: Most links use the repeated generic label “こちら” (“here”).
findings.evidence: The DOM probe lists seven of eight anchors with identical text “こちら”, obscuring destination and purpose when scanned or read out of context.
findings.suggestedFix: Use destination-specific link text such as “即PATの受付時間” and “投票履歴を確認” while keeping real href values.

findings.summary: Indexing endpoints and canonical signals are malformed or absent.
findings.evidence: /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml return the service notice as 200 text/html; Lighthouse reports 83 robots.txt errors, and the DOM has no canonical URL.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve valid text/plain robots.txt and XML sitemap responses, add a canonical link, and preserve truthful HTTP status/content types during service downtime.

findings.summary: The public service notice has no structured or social-preview metadata.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe finds zero JSON-LD blocks and zero Open Graph properties.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Open Graph metadata and minimal Organization/WebSite JSON-LD consistent with visible JRA content.

findings.summary: HTTPS is used, but all audited defensive response headers are absent.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive reports no CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy HSTS, nosniff, a restrictive CSP including frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy after staged compatibility testing.

findings.summary: Small decorative raster assets lack modern/resolution-aware variants.
findings.evidence: The images primitive finds two legacy PNG images, no modern formats, and no srcset for the larger logo; Lighthouse flags low-resolution responsive image delivery.
findings.suggestedFix: Prefer SVG for logos or provide appropriately sized 1x/2x AVIF/WebP/image-set variants, while retaining intrinsic dimensions.

taskList.title: Make the entry/status page genuinely responsive and legible on mobile
Deploy layered security headers for the transaction origin
Fix alert contrast and semantic page structure
Serve truthful HTTP status, robots, sitemap, and canonical signals
Move the response into standards mode with modern metadata
Reduce root latency and cache versioned static assets
Respect the user’s dark color-scheme preference
